### Description

This fail might cause an issue. This PR's approach doesn't work well in a concurrent situation.
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/actions/runs/4292613465/jobs/7479273031#step:13:105

I guess this fail happened by the following steps:

1. playground A: `net.connect` checks port 5173 => success
2. playground B: `net.connect` checks port 5173 => success
3. playground A: listen port 5173
4. playground B: listen port 5173 => error

Umm, it failed 3 out of 7 times.
In this way, concurrency seems to be inevitable, and better methods need to be found 🤔

issue_context.title: Dev servers are opened in identical ports
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Multiple development servers are opened in `http://localhost:5173/`.

Related https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/12144

### Reproduction

https://github.com/vitejs/vite

### Steps to reproduce

In macOS, open a terminal window.

Open two tabs, each in different directories.

```
a % npm i vite -D

added 15 packages in 2s

4 packages are looking for funding
  run `npm fund` for details
a % npx vite dev

  VITE v4.1.4  ready in 205 ms

  ➜  Local:   http://localhost:5173/
  ➜  Network: use --host to expose
  ➜  press h to show help
(!) Could not auto-determine entry point from rollupOptions or html files and there are no explicit optimizeDeps.include patterns. Skipping dependency pre-bundling.
```

↕️ Both are opened in `http://localhost:5173/`

```
b % npm i vite -D

added 15 packages in 437ms

4 packages are looking for funding
  run `npm fund` for details
b % npx vite dev --host

  VITE v4.1.4  ready in 192 ms

  ➜  Local:   http://localhost:5173/
  ➜  Network: http://192.168.68.113:5173/
  ➜  press h to show help
(!) Could not auto-determine entry point from rollupOptions or html files and there are no explicit optimizeDeps.include patterns. Skipping dependency pre-bundling.
```

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 13.2.1
    CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M1 Pro
    Memory: 104.98 MB / 16.00 GB
    Shell: 5.8.1 - /bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 18.14.2 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v18.14.2/bin/node
    npm: 9.5.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v18.14.2/bin/npm
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

comments:
According to my test:

Set -- host, and then `httpServer.listen` passes the host as `undefined`, and do not set the pass `localhost`

I start the first service, and when `-- host` is not delivered http://127.0.0.1:5173/ 、http://localhost:5173/ are effective

Then start the second service and pass -- host, `http://localhost:5173/` Covered by the second service, `http://127.0.0.1:5173/ `Still occupied by the first service

review_comments: I think it would be nice to have a comment that describes that this code tries to establish a tcp connection instead of trying to listen a port.

Interesting approach. I'm a bit worried about the inverted logic here. Are we sure that `connect` only fails when the port is unused? Could a used port still reject the connection making this logic invalid?

I looked up a lot of data. It is only the IP or port number with invalid connection that fails.
Of course, I can't guarantee that this is correct.
I tested Node16 and Node18 in Windows and Mac, and they all work normally
